analysis:
Compared the complete supplied BASE/HEAD publication script and examined all test source, metadata and bounded patch evidence. scripts/provider-release-publication.py:71-185 adds strict cluster-fact schema, nonzero digest, placement, envelope, ordering and canonical-JSON checks; :215-228 bounds derived IDs and the actual registration body. prepare attaches optional facts before retained payload creation (:247-275); stage/publish revalidate them (:329-338, :367-377). Existing signed-bundle hash checking, production source/tag verification, bearer authentication, redirect refusal and readiness-before-alias publication remain intact. No independently supported security regression was identified.

The new facts carry pair-serving grants and parity qualification evidence, relevant to A-004, A-011, A-017, T-027, T-054 and T-056. Validation checks structure, not evidence authenticity or binding to the signed runtime. Integration must verify the facts generator/workflow establishes that binding and that platform approval consumption preserves qualification and revocation controls; this script alone does not establish their absence. The model-fetch tests (scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py:91-288) exercise identity/config binding, modality validation, redirects, response bounds, retry behavior and fail-before-output behavior, but the imported fetch implementation is not supplied here and tests were not executed. Pipeline-test patch evidence changes failure expectations for optional facts computation and diagnostic retention (scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py:209-215); actual workflow gating needs reconciliation with publication's optional block. Only metadata and bounded patch context were supplied for that modified test file. Cluster approval semantics may require threat-model expansion if this lane enables distributed serving; activation and runtime behavior cannot be inferred from these units. No prompt, key, cache, fan-helper, logout or billing runtime changes are visible in this scope.
